purpose: Small synthetic receipt-entry suggestion acceptance corpus; no actual user receipt data.
expectationScope: Optional useful suggestions only. Never auto-select, rewrite raw description, or require review. Candidate retrieval is not identity verification.

cases.reason: Only a package number overlaps; unrelated product.
Number and weight unit do not identify beans.
Same mass does not establish a useful product relationship.
Exact name supports an optional suggestion.
Approved description is advisory evidence across store/code change; exact-source rule must not transfer.
Product-bearing whole word supports a useful alternative without claiming exact identity.
Product name provides useful optional grouping; package identity remains unconfirmed.
Both are plausible alternatives; no automatic choice or invented confidence.
Short exact product name remains useful.
Unapproved abbreviation is not identity evidence just because its letters occur inside rubber.
Shared substring alone does not establish the same product or a useful alternative.
A store item code is not a global product identity.
Two shared product words identify the product; one shared word with a two-word name does not.
Word order does not matter; a shared origin word alone is not product evidence.
A whole product word can match a generic one-word name; a different word form is not a whole-word match.

measurement.method: Report each named case as pass/fail against offered and rejected sets, preserving raw description and optional continuation. Count false offers separately from missed useful suggestions. Record backend retrieval separately from visible UI and distinguish debounced-query mismatch.
measurement.limits: This is a regression corpus, not a representative accuracy benchmark. No scored confidence, universal correctness, provider comparison, or live usage conclusion is supported. Expand using consented redacted examples before choosing broader quality targets.
